c.tagline: Theme-park magic under endless Florida sun

emergency.note: 911 covers police, fire and ambulance; English-speaking operators are standard, with translation services available.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Downtown Orlando: Lake Eola Park with its fountain and swan boats
hood_landmark.Winter Park: the Morse Museum's world-famous Tiffany glass collection on Park Avenue
hood_landmark.Lake Nona: Boxi Park, the open-air shipping-container dining and entertainment village
hood_landmark.International Drive: ICON Park and its 400-foot observation wheel

avoid.reason: Tourists have little reason to enter Pine Hills, Parramore or the Mercy Drive corridor, which see notably higher violent crime, especially after dark.
Watch for car break-ins in theme-park and outlet-mall lots, and keep usual awareness on South Orange Blossom Trail and quieter stretches of International Drive late at night.

hood_desc: Downtown Orlando is the walkable urban core around Lake Eola with high-rises, bars along Orange Avenue and nightlife, suited to travelers wanting city energy away from the theme parks.
Winter Park is an upscale, tree-lined suburb of brick streets, Park Avenue boutiques, museums and lakeside charm, ideal for refined, relaxed stays and culture lovers.
Lake Nona is a modern, master-planned community near the airport known for its medical city, sports campus and sleek new hotels, appealing to business and contemporary travelers.
International Drive is the tourist strip of hotels, outlet malls, the ICON Park Ferris wheel and convention center, a convenient budget-to-mid base close to the attractions.
lodging: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Winter Park
Residence Inn by Marriott Orlando Lake Nona
Courtyard by Marriott Orlando Lake Nona

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: LYNX buses cost $2 per ride or $4.50 for a day pass, paid with exact cash on board or via the LYNX PawPass app. SunRail tickets and reloadable SunCards come from station vending machines; the downtown LYMMO bus loop is free. The I-Ride Trolley on International Drive takes $2 cash.
transit.hours: Most LYNX routes run roughly 5am-11pm; SunRail runs weekdays only (about 5:30am-11pm) with no weekend service.
transit.note: Transit is thin outside downtown and I-Drive - most visitors rely on a rental car, Uber/Lyft, hotel theme-park shuttles, and the I-Ride Trolley.

transit.m: Lynx bus 11 to downtown Orlando (45 min)

food.name: Cuban sandwich
food.desc: Pressed pork, ham, Swiss, pickle and mustard on Cuban bread. Central Florida's Latin population makes it as much an Orlando staple as a Miami one.

places.name: Black Bean Deli
places.note: Voted Orlando Weekly's Best Cuban Sandwich 2025; also excellent ham croquetas and cafe con leche.

places.name: Cuban Sandwiches To Go
places.note: No-frills counter praised for the proper crunch and tender mojo pork; cheap and fast.

places.name: Zaza New Cuban Diner
places.note: Third-generation family kitchen with a modern diner spin; several branches across metro Orlando.

food.name: Gator bites
food.desc: Cubes of alligator tail, buttermilk-battered and fried, served with remoulade. The classic Florida-swamp appetizer.

places.name: Gator's Dockside
places.note: Local sports-bar chain and the easiest reliable gator tail in town; also good for a game night.

places.name: Tibby's New Orleans Kitchen
places.note: Cajun kitchen with fried gator, po'boys and beignets in a cheerful, family-friendly room.

places.name: Pearl's Good Eats at Gatorland
places.note: Famous gator nuggets inside the old-school gator park; combine it with the attraction itself.

food.name: Mofongo and Puerto Rican classics
food.desc: Green plantain pounded in a pilon with garlic and pork, loaded with shrimp or pernil. Central Florida has a huge Puerto Rican community.

places.name: Chimiking
places.note: Called Orlando's mofongo paradise; hand-mashed in the pilon and topped to order, from garlic shrimp to surf and turf.

places.name: Tropico Mofongo
places.note: Caribbean kitchen near the parks with a mofongo-led menu and generous portions.

places.name: 787 Mofongo
places.note: Widely rated the best Puerto Rican food truck in Central Florida; check social media for the day's stop.

food.name: Vietnamese pho and banh mi
food.desc: Twelve-hour beef broth and crackly baguette sandwiches in the Mills 50 district, Orlando's Little Saigon and its best-kept food secret.

places.name: Banh Mi Boy
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025; crispy pork belly with roast garlic mayo and pate, plus a pho-broth French dip.

places.name: Pho 2 To
places.note: Bones simmered over 12 hours with charred ginger and toasted spice for a clean, deep broth.

places.name: Pho Huong Lan
places.note: Long-running neighbourhood staple and unofficial community hangout; unfussy and consistent.

food.name: Key lime pie
food.desc: Tart custard of key lime juice and condensed milk in a graham crust. A Florida birthright dessert, done properly well inland.

places.name: Sister Honey's
places.note: James Beard-nominated baker making pie from scratch daily with hand-squeezed key lime juice.

places.name: Lombardi's Seafood
places.note: Homemade pie from a 60-year-old family recipe, and one of the better-value whole pies in town.

places.name: Lighthouse Seafood Market and Cafe
places.note: Family recipe with hand-whipped cream; a proper seafood-shack setting for it.

food.name: Dole Whip
food.desc: Soft-serve pineapple whip, dairy-free and impossibly refreshing in Florida heat. A theme-park ritual locals happily admit to loving.

places.name: Aloha Isle
places.note: The original walk-up window; get it as a float in pineapple juice. Expect a queue in the afternoon.

places.name: Pineapple Lanai
places.note: Same treat without a park ticket, plus a monorail ride and a tiki-themed lobby.

food.name: Butterbeer
food.desc: Butterscotch-shortbread cream soda with a thick foam cap, served frozen, cold, hot or as an ice bar. Non-alcoholic and only found here.

places.name: Three Broomsticks
places.note: Sit-down version with a fire-lit interior; frozen Butterbeer from the Magic Neep cart nearby.

places.name: The Leaky Cauldron
places.note: Best paired with a Butterbeer potted cream dessert; the alley itself is worth the visit.

places.name: The Hopping Pot
places.note: Walk-up counter for frozen Butterbeer plus the wizarding beers if you want something stronger.

food.name: Local craft beer
food.desc: Orlando has over a dozen breweries inside city limits, leaning to crisp pilsners and tropical hops that suit the climate.

places.name: Ivanhoe Park Brewing Company
places.note: Award-winning pilsners and a rotating tap list in an industrial-chic taproom just north of downtown.

places.name: Crooked Can Brewing Company
places.note: Anchors Plant Street Market, a food hall with 20-plus vendors in a historic downtown; great half-day trip.

places.name: Hourglass Brewing
places.note: Experimental local favourite with an easygoing neighbourhood crowd and frequent food trucks.

landmarks: Cinderella Castle
Magic Kingdom's fairy-tale centerpiece and one of the most photographed structures in the world.
Spaceship Earth (Epcot)
Epcot's giant geodesic sphere is an unmistakable architectural icon and symbol of the park.
Hogwarts Castle (Islands of Adventure)
The meticulously detailed Wizarding World castle draws Harry Potter fans for its dramatic, film-accurate silhouette.
Tree of Life (Animal Kingdom)
A massive sculpted tree with hundreds of carved animals, forming the visual anchor of Disney's Animal Kingdom.
Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
A short drive from Orlando, this NASA complex offers dramatic rocket displays including the Space Shuttle Atlantis.
Lake Eola Park
Downtown Orlando's picturesque lake with swan paddleboats and a fountain framed by the city skyline.
Gatorland
A classic Florida attraction showcasing thousands of alligators and crocodiles amid swampy, photogenic scenery.
The Wheel at ICON Park
A 400-foot observation wheel offering panoramic sunset views over Orlando's International Drive.
Universal Studios Florida
Home to the iconic rotating globe entrance and movie-themed streets that define the resort's brand.
Discovery Cove
A tranquil, all-inclusive tropical resort-style park known for its lagoons and dolphin encounters, a favorite for scenic shots.

train.note: No international trains run from the US Southeast. Amtrak's long-distance Floridian (Chicago-Pittsburgh-Washington-Miami) and Silver Meteor (New York-Miami) call at Orlando's downtown station on Sligh Boulevard, and the Auto Train to the Washington DC area (Lorton, VA) leaves from Sanford, about 40 minutes north. The fastest option to South Florida is Brightline, which runs from its own station at Orlando International Airport to West Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale and Miami in around 3.5 hours. SunRail commuter trains link downtown with DeBary, Sanford and Poinciana on weekdays only.

bus.note: No international coach routes from Orlando; reaching Mexico or Canada by bus means several changes. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) run to Miami, Tampa and Jacksonville from the terminal at 555 N John Young Parkway, west of downtown and awkward to reach without a taxi. RedCoach (https://www.redcoachusa.com/) runs premium reclining-seat coaches within Florida. Miami takes 4-5 hours and Tampa about 2; fares are cheapest booked online well in advance.

ferry.note: Orlando is inland with no ferry services. The nearest port, Port Canaveral about 45 minutes east, handles cruise ships only - there are no scheduled passenger ferries.

half.name: St. Augustine
half.blurb: America's oldest city, brimming with Spanish colonial architecture, a stone fort, and cobbled streets.

half.name: Cocoa Beach
half.blurb: A classic surf town with a landmark pier and wide sandy Atlantic shoreline.

half.name: Clearwater Beach
half.blurb: Powdery white sand and turquoise Gulf waters make this a beloved seaside escape.

half.name: Crystal River
half.blurb: Famous spring-fed waters where visitors can swim alongside gentle wild manatees.

half.name: Daytona Beach
half.blurb: Miles of hard-packed drivable sand plus the legendary international speedway nearby.

half.name: Blue Spring State Park
half.blurb: A crystal-clear spring and winter manatee refuge perfect for swimming and paddling.
